THIS WEEK IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT

Marathon County supervisors overhauled animal waste rules after an 18-month farmer-conservation partnership and advanced a resolution pressing Alliant Energy on its Hub City Wind project, while Wausau and DC Everest school districts and multiple municipalities tackled budgets, benefits, and land use.

  • Marathon County Board approved Ordinance 41-26 updating animal waste management rules after 18 months of collaboration with farmers and conservation groups; winter spreading restrictions take effect in 2028.
  • The Marathon County Executive Committee voted 8-2 to forward a resolution directing Alliant Energy to submit a Hub City Wind agreement addressing township concerns by November 1, 2025.
  • Wausau's joint HR and Finance committees approved a 2027 employee benefit package featuring higher deductibles and premium increases; the HR committee separately voted to terminate an ATU Local 1168 employee following a closed-session grievance review.
  • DC Everest School Board approved a 19.1% health insurance premium increase with Aspirus Health Plan for 2027 and received updates on relocating IDEA and Odyssey alternative schools amid declining enrollment.
  • Wausau's Board of Public Works approved a $109,500 change order for PFAS water treatment flooring work and received four engineering proposals for Bridge Street intersection signal design, to be reviewed at a future meeting.
  • Weston's Plan Commission found Bug Properties on Schofield Avenue out of compliance with its conditional use permit and set a September 23 deadline for site improvements before a potential public hearing.

Coming up: The full Marathon County Board meets Tuesday, September 22 at 7:00 p.m. and is expected to take up the Hub City Wind resolution forwarded by the Executive Committee; Wausau's Finance Committee also meets Tuesday at 5:15 p.m. as the city continues budget season deliberations.
